question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I have been working here for years."'

options.A: He said that he had been working there for years.
options.B: He said that he has been working here for years.
options.C: He said that he was working there for years.
options.D: He said that he had worked there for years.

explanation: Present perfect continuous ('have been working') shifts to past perfect continuous ('had been working'), and 'here' shifts to 'there'.

question: Spot the error: 'He asked me that why I didn't come to the party.'

options.A: He asked me
options.B: that why
options.C: I didn't come
options.D: to the party.

explanation: Do not use 'that' before a WH- question word in indirect speech. Correct: 'He asked me why I didn't come...'

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'The doctor said to the patient, "Take your medicine regularly."'

options.A: The doctor told the patient to take his medicine regularly.
options.B: The doctor advised the patient to take his medicine regularly.
options.C: The doctor suggested the patient to take his medicine regularly.
options.D: Both A and B are correct.

explanation: Both 'told' and 'advised' are appropriate reporting verbs for this imperative/advice structure.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Alas! We have lost the match."'

options.A: She exclaimed with sorrow that they had lost the match.
options.B: She said with sorrow that we have lost the match.
options.C: She cried out that we lost the match.
options.D: She exclaimed that they have lost the match.

explanation: Grief exclamations ('Alas!') shift to 'exclaimed with sorrow' and tenses backshift ('have lost' -> 'had lost').

question: Spot the error: 'The manager said that he will look into the matter.'

options.A: The manager said
options.B: that he will look
options.C: into the matter.
options.D: No error

explanation: Past reporting verb ('said') requires 'will' to change to the past form 'would'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I can run very fast."'

options.A: He said that he can run very fast.
options.B: He said that he could run very fast.
options.C: He said that he was able to run very fast.
options.D: Both B and C are correct.

explanation: Modal 'can' shifts to 'could' or 'was able to' in indirect speech.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Is it raining?"'

options.A: She asked if it was raining.
options.B: She asked was it raining.
options.C: She asked that if it was raining.
options.D: She asked whether was it raining.

explanation: Yes/no questions use 'if/whether' and declarative word order ('it was raining').

question: Spot the error: 'He inquired me of the time.'

options.A: He inquired me
options.B: of the time.
options.C: No error
options.D: None

explanation: 'Inquire' requires 'of' before the object ('He inquired of me the time').

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Good morning, my dear friend!"'

options.A: He wished his dear friend good morning.
options.B: He said good morning to his dear friend.
options.C: He greeted his dear friend good morning.
options.D: All of the above are correct.

explanation: Various ways to express greetings are grammatically acceptable in reported speech.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Must you go?"'

options.A: She asked if I must go.
options.B: She asked if I had to go.
options.C: She asked must I go.
options.D: She inquired that had I to go.

explanation: 'Must' indicating necessity changes to 'had to' in indirect speech.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Honesty is the best policy."'

options.A: He said that honesty was the best policy.
options.B: He said that honesty is the best policy.
options.C: He told honesty is the best policy.
options.D: He asked if honesty is the best policy.

explanation: Universal truths/proverbs remain in the present tense even when the reporting verb is past.

question: Spot the error: 'She told me that she will have finished the report by then.'

options.A: She told me that
options.B: she will have finished
options.C: the report by then.
options.D: No error

explanation: Past reporting verb ('told') requires the future perfect ('will have finished') to shift to its past form ('would have finished').

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Bravo! You have done a great job."'

options.A: She applauded him saying that he had done a great job.
options.B: She exclaimed with sorrow that he did a great job.
options.C: She said that bravo he has done a great job.
options.D: She told him to do a great job.

explanation: Bravo is an exclamation of praise, converted with 'applauded him saying that...' and backshifting tenses.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Let's have some tea."'

options.A: He proposed that they should have some tea.
options.B: He suggested having some tea.
options.C: Both A and B are correct.
options.D: Neither is correct.

explanation: Both 'suggested + gerund' and 'proposed + that... should...' are valid forms for suggestions.

question: Spot the error: 'The guard ordered the thief to not move.'

options.A: The guard ordered
options.B: the thief
options.C: to not move.
options.D: No error

explanation: Negative imperatives in indirect speech use 'not to move', not 'to not move'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "I have been ill since Monday."'

options.A: She said that she had been ill since Monday.
options.B: She said that she has been ill since Monday.
options.C: She said that she was ill since Monday.
options.D: She said that she was being ill since Monday.

explanation: Present perfect continuous ('have been') shifts to past perfect continuous ('had been') in indirect speech.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He asked me, "Do you know where the hotel is?"'

options.A: He asked me if I knew where the hotel was.
options.B: He asked me that if I know where the hotel is.
options.C: He asked me did I know where the hotel was.
options.D: He asked me where I knew the hotel is.

explanation: Yes/no question ('if I knew...') with tense backshift ('know' -> 'knew', 'is' -> 'was').

question: Spot the error: 'He asked me where I was living last year.'

options.A: He asked me
options.B: where I was living
options.C: last year.
options.D: No error

explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. Past continuous can be used in reported speech for past states.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "What a terrible disaster!"'

options.A: He exclaimed that it was a terrible disaster.
options.B: He said that what a terrible disaster.
options.C: He shouted that it is a terrible disaster.
options.D: He asked what a terrible disaster was.

explanation: Exclamatory sentences convert using 'exclaimed' + 'it was...'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'The principal said, "Boys, do not make a noise."'

options.A: The principal ordered the boys not to make a noise.
options.B: The principal told to the boys to not make a noise.
options.C: The principal requested that boys do not make a noise.
options.D: The principal said the boys not to make a noise.

explanation: Imperative negative conversion: 'ordered... not to [verb]'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "I have been working."'

options.A: She said that she had been working.
options.B: She said that she has been working.
options.C: She said she was working.
options.D: She said that she has worked.

explanation: Present perfect continuous ('have been working') shifts to past perfect continuous ('had been working').

question: Spot the error: 'The traveler asked how far was the city.'

options.A: The traveler asked
options.B: how far was the city.
options.C: No error
options.D: None

explanation: Indirect questions require declarative order: 'how far the city was'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I would like to have a coffee."'

options.A: He said that he would like to have a coffee.
options.B: He said that he will like to have a coffee.
options.C: He said that he likes to have a coffee.
options.D: He said that he had liked to have a coffee.

explanation: 'Would' as an auxiliary verb often remains unchanged in indirect speech.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'The mother said, "May you live long, my child!"'

options.A: The mother wished that her child might live long.
options.B: The mother prayed that her child may live long.
options.C: The mother told the child to live long.
options.D: The mother asked if the child lives long.

explanation: Prayers convert using 'wished/prayed' + subject + 'might' + base verb.

question: Spot the error: 'He suggested that I should to go there.'

options.A: He suggested that
options.B: I should to go
options.C: there.
options.D: No error

explanation: 'Should' is a modal and takes the bare infinitive ('go'), not the full infinitive ('to go').

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "I'll see you tomorrow."'

options.A: She said that she would see me the next day.
options.B: She said that she will see me the next day.
options.C: She said that she would see me tomorrow.
options.D: She said that she should see me the next day.

explanation: 'Will' shifts to 'would', and 'tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "Do you like apples?"'

options.A: He asked me if I liked apples.
options.B: He asked me do I like apples.
options.C: He said if I liked apples.
options.D: He asked me that if I liked apples.

explanation: Simple present yes/no question ('Do you like...') becomes simple past declarative ('if I liked').

question: Spot the error: 'The boy said that he done his work.'

options.A: The boy said that
options.B: he done
options.C: his work.
options.D: No error

explanation: Reported speech after 'said' requires past perfect ('had done') or at least simple past ('did') if the timeline was clear, but 'done' without an auxiliary is incorrect.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Oh! I missed the train."'

options.A: She exclaimed with regret that she had missed the train.
options.B: She exclaimed with joy that she missed the train.
options.C: She said that she missed the train.
options.D: She said that she has missed the train.

explanation: Exclamations of regret use 'exclaimed with regret', with backshifting ('missed' -> 'had missed').

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'They said, "We live in London."'

options.A: They said that they lived in London.
options.B: They said that they live in London.
options.C: They said that we lived in London.
options.D: They said that we live in London.

explanation: Simple present 'live' shifts to past 'lived', and 'We' shifts to 'they'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I have been ill since Monday."'

options.A: He said that he had been ill since Monday.
options.B: He said that he has been ill since Monday.
options.C: He said that he was ill since Monday.
options.D: He said that he had been ill till Monday.

explanation: Present perfect 'have been' shifts to past perfect 'had been'.

question: Spot the error: 'The manager said he has to meet the client.'

options.A: The manager said
options.B: he has to meet
options.C: the client.
options.D: No error

explanation: Past reporting verb 'said' requires backshift of 'has to' to 'had to'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Must you go so soon?"'

options.A: She asked if I had to go so soon.
options.B: She asked if I must go so soon.
options.C: She asked did I have to go so soon.
options.D: She asked if I would have to go so soon.

explanation: Necessity 'must' shifts to 'had to' in indirect speech.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said to me, "You should apologize."'

options.A: He advised me to apologize.
options.B: He said that I should apologize.
options.C: Both A and B are correct.
options.D: Neither is correct.

explanation: Both forms ('He advised me to...' and 'He said that I should...') are correct.

question: Spot the error: 'The teacher said that the sun rose in the east.'

options.A: The teacher said that
options.B: the sun rose
options.C: in the east.
options.D: No error

explanation: Universal truths ('sun rises') do not shift tense even after 'said'. It should be 'rises'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Alas! My dog died."'

options.A: She exclaimed with sorrow that her dog had died.
options.B: She said with sorrow that her dog died.
options.C: She exclaimed that her dog died.
options.D: She exclaimed with joy that her dog died.

explanation: Backshift required ('died' -> 'had died') for past actions.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "What are you doing?"'

options.A: He asked what I was doing.
options.B: He asked what I am doing.
options.C: He asked what was I doing.
options.D: He asked me what I am doing.

explanation: Indirect WH- questions require declarative word order ('I was doing') and tense backshift.

question: Spot the error: 'He asked me where did I live.'

options.A: He asked me
options.B: where did I live.
options.C: No error
options.D: None

explanation: Indirect questions require declarative word order. 'Where I lived'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I have just come from school."'

options.A: He said that he had just come from school.
options.B: He said that he has just come from school.
options.C: He said that he just came from school.
options.D: He said that he would just come from school.

explanation: Present perfect 'have just come' shifts to past perfect 'had just come'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "I will never see his face again."'

options.A: She said that she would never see his face again.
options.B: She said that she will never see his face again.
options.C: She said that she would never saw his face again.
options.D: She said that she never saw his face again.

explanation: 'Will' shifts to 'would', rest remains unchanged.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said to me, "You can stay here."'

options.A: He told me that I could stay there.
options.B: He told me that I can stay there.
options.C: He told me that I could stay here.
options.D: He told me that I should stay there.

explanation: 'Can' shifts to 'could', and 'here' shifts to 'there'.

question: Spot the error: 'The manager said he would call me tomorrow.'

options.A: The manager said
options.B: he would call me
options.C: tomorrow.
options.D: No error

explanation: 'Tomorrow' should be shifted to 'the next day' in indirect speech.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Is he working today?"'

options.A: She asked if he was working that day.
options.B: She asked if he is working today.
options.C: She asked was he working that day.
options.D: She asked if he was working today.

explanation: Yes/no question ('if'), backshift ('is' -> 'was'), and time shift ('today' -> 'that day').

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I have finished my project."'

options.A: He said that he had finished his project.
options.B: He said that he has finished his project.
options.C: He said that he finished his project.
options.D: He said that he has had finished his project.

explanation: Present perfect 'have finished' shifts to past perfect 'had finished'.

question: Spot the error: 'He said that he is going to the market.'

options.A: He said that
options.B: he is going
options.C: to the market.
options.D: No error

explanation: Reporting verb 'said' requires backshift. It should be 'was going'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said to me, "Where are you going?"'

options.A: She asked me where I was going.
options.B: She asked me where was I going.
options.C: She asked me where am I going.
options.D: She told me where I was going.

explanation: WH- question indirect form: declarative order ('I was going').

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I shall work hard."'

options.A: He said that he would work hard.
options.B: He said that he should work hard.
options.C: He said that he shall work hard.
options.D: He said that he will work hard.

explanation: 'Shall' in indirect speech shifts to 'would' (reflecting the change from 'shall' to 'will' in the future prediction).

question: Spot the error: 'She told me that the sky is blue.'

options.A: She told me that
options.B: the sky is
options.C: blue.
options.D: No error

explanation: Universal truths retain present tense ('is blue'). Sentence is correct.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'She said, "Please pass the salt."'

options.A: She requested me to pass the salt.
options.B: She requested to pass the salt.
options.C: She said to pass the salt.
options.D: She told me please pass the salt.

explanation: 'Please' requests convert to 'requested + object + to + infinitive'.

question: Convert into indirect speech: 'He said, "I know him."'

options.A: He said that he knew him.
options.B: He said that he knows him.
options.C: He told that he knew him.
options.D: He asked if he knew him.

explanation: Simple present 'know' shifts to simple past 'knew'.
